## Pre-Difficulty Gate Failed

Difficulty not run: the submission did not pass every blocking quality or quality panel check. Oracle/NOP already passed. No Opus, GPT, analysis, or rubric-generation runs were started.

QUALITY PANEL: NEEDS REVISION -- 3 blocking issues to fix. Details for each are below.

Blocking (fix every one):
   1. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR: The verifier imposes an undisclosed 2,000,000-byte
      schedule-file limit, rejecting valid JSON representations without changing their
      assignments or cost.
   2. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: Ordinary JSON loading erases duplicate press-ID keys, so the
      verifier cannot enforce the rule that each press key occurs at most once.
   3. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: Duplicate press keys in the JSON text are accepted because
      json.load discards all but the last occurrence before the verifier checks press keys.

Checked and clean: Correct Reference Solution, Protected Ground Truth, Deterministic Execution.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DETAILS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR -- hidden grading semantics
   The verifier imposes an undisclosed 2,000,000-byte schedule-file limit, rejecting valid JSON
   representations without changing their assignments or cost.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: The candidate controls /app/schedules/week-36.json, which both week-36 tests read.
     Serialize a feasible week-36 schedule compactly into L bytes and append exactly 2,000,001-L
     ASCII spaces. For example, the shipped planner produces a feasible assignment of the week's
     45 jobs whose compact representation is far below the ceiling; padding this file preserves
     feasibility. For Reviewer 1's construction, the same transformation applies to any
     target-meeting schedule and preserves its target-meeting cost. Flip: At
     tests/test_outputs.py:32 the existing regular file passes isfile; at line 33 getsize
     returns 2,000,001, so the comparison against MAX_BYTES=2,000,000 is false. Execution stops
     before json.load at line 35 and evaluate at line 37. Thus test_week_36_schedule_is_valid
     changes from passing for the compact feasible schedule to failing for the padded
     representation. A target-meeting schedule also loses its target-test pass. In contrast, the
     candidate-visible checker directly calls json.load at lines 76–77, which consumes trailing
     JSON whitespace, and evaluates the unchanged parsed object at line 79. I checked
     instruction.md, task.toml, the Dockerfile, environment/app/README.md, docs/press-rules.md,
     the shipped planner and checker, and all supplied week and target files: none states a
     file-size limit. No contract clause excludes the padded representation.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/press-rules.md:48-55,
     environment/app/tools/check_schedule.py:74-84, tests/test_outputs.py:22,
     tests/test_outputs.py:30-39, tests/test_outputs.py:47-52

2. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- partial output validation
   Ordinary JSON loading erases duplicate press-ID keys, so the verifier cannot enforce the rule
   that each press key occurs at most once.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Take any four schedules that pass the cost checks, and in week-36.json insert `"P1":
     [],` immediately before its existing `"P1": [...]` entry, leaving the existing entry and
     all other schedules unchanged. Flip: Python's json.load retains the latter P1 list, so
     evaluate receives exactly the original schedule; all validity and target assertions retain
     their passing results. The written week-36 file nevertheless gives the P1 key twice,
     contrary to the file-format rule. This is a deliberately crafted parser-boundary bypass,
     not an omission a normal schedule writer is likely to produce.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/press-rules.md:50-55, tests/test_outputs.py:30-39,
     tests/check_schedule.py:34-42

3. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- partial output validation
   Duplicate press keys in the JSON text are accepted because json.load discards all but the
   last occurrence before the verifier checks press keys.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Take any of the four below-target schedules and serialize its presses object with
     `"P1":[]` immediately before its existing `"P1":<original list>`; if P1 was omitted, use
     `"P1":[],"P1":[]`. Keep every other member unchanged. This is a schedule file giving P1
     twice, contrary to the format rule. Flip: json.load retains only the second P1 value. The
     evaluator therefore sees exactly the original assignments (or the same empty P1), clears
     every feasibility check, and computes exactly the original below-target cost. No assertion
     examines duplicate keys in the source text. This is a deliberate parser-specific
     construction, rather than an ordinary way to generate the schedules.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/press-rules.md:50-53, tests/test_outputs.py:30-37,
     tests/check_schedule.py:30-43, tests/test_outputs.py:42-44

✅ pass - difficult: The problem is unrelated-parallel-machine scheduling with sequence-dependent setups, tonnage eligibility, release times, weighted tardiness, and hard maintenance windows — a genuine combinatorial optimization problem requiring OR/metaheuristic expertise (ruin-and-recreate, simulated annealing, local search) to beat a naive EDD dispatcher by 2-4x, as documented.
✅ pass - interesting: This is a realistic stamping-line production-scheduling problem (die changeovers, tonnage classes, maintenance windows, weighted tardiness) that production planners and OR engineers are paid to solve in manufacturing settings.

1. [Coherent Contract] MAJOR -- hidden grading semantics
   The verifier imposes an undisclosed 2,000,000-byte schedule-file limit, rejecting valid JSON
   representations without changing their assignments or cost.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: The candidate controls /app/schedules/week-36.json, which both week-36 tests read.
     Serialize a feasible week-36 schedule compactly into L bytes and append exactly 2,000,001-L
     ASCII spaces. For example, the shipped planner produces a feasible assignment of the week's
     45 jobs whose compact representation is far below the ceiling; padding this file preserves
     feasibility. For Reviewer 1's construction, the same transformation applies to any
     target-meeting schedule and preserves its target-meeting cost. Flip: At
     tests/test_outputs.py:32 the existing regular file passes isfile; at line 33 getsize
     returns 2,000,001, so the comparison against MAX_BYTES=2,000,000 is false. Execution stops
     before json.load at line 35 and evaluate at line 37. Thus test_week_36_schedule_is_valid
     changes from passing for the compact feasible schedule to failing for the padded
     representation. A target-meeting schedule also loses its target-test pass. In contrast, the
     candidate-visible checker directly calls json.load at lines 76–77, which consumes trailing
     JSON whitespace, and evaluates the unchanged parsed object at line 79. I checked
     instruction.md, task.toml, the Dockerfile, environment/app/README.md, docs/press-rules.md,
     the shipped planner and checker, and all supplied week and target files: none states a
     file-size limit. No contract clause excludes the padded representation.

     environment/app/tools/check_schedule.py:74-84, tests/test_outputs.py:22,
     tests/test_outputs.py:30-39, tests/test_outputs.py:47-52

2. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- partial output validation
   Ordinary JSON loading erases duplicate press-ID keys, so the verifier cannot enforce the rule
   that each press key occurs at most once.
